name: LT6230CS6#TRPBF
title: LT6230/LT6230-10/LT6231/LT6232: 215 MHz, rail-to-rail output, 1.1 nV/√Hz, 3.5 mA op amp family
summary: Low-noise voltage-feedback op amps with a bipolar input pair and rail-to-rail output: 1.1 nV/√Hz at 10 kHz on 3.15 mA typical (3.5 mA maximum) per amplifier. LT6230 (single, with shutdown), LT6231 (dual) and LT6232 (quad) are unity-gain stable with 200 MHz to 215 MHz gain-bandwidth; LT6230-10 is a single stable at gains of 10 and up with 1300 MHz to 1450 MHz. Supplies run 3 V to 12.6 V; the output reaches within 50 mV of each rail and the singles shut down to under 10 µA. C grade 0 °C to 70 °C, I grade −40 °C to 85 °C.
key_figures: 1.1 nV/√Hz typ, 1.7 nV/√Hz max at 10 kHz; 180 nVP-P 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz
1 pA/√Hz balanced, 2.4 pA/√Hz unbalanced at 10 kHz
3.15 mA typ, 3.5 mA max per amplifier (5 V, 25 °C); under 10 µA disabled (LT6230, LT6230-10)
50 µV typ, 350 µV max (LT6231S8, LT6232GN); 500 µV max (LT6230S6)
50 mV max from either rail unloaded; ±45 mA short-circuit typ (5 V)

notes: The tape-and-reel numbers of the LT6231 SO-8 read LT6230CS8#TRPBF and LT6230IS8#TRPBF; by the pattern of the rest they are LT6231CS8#TRPBF and LT6231IS8#TRPBF.

LT6230 is the single, LT6231 the dual and LT6232 the quad, all unity-gain stable. LT6230-10 is a single compensated for gains of 10 or more, with higher gain-bandwidth and slew rate. Only the LT6230 and LT6230-10 have the ENABLE pin.
The temperature grade is marked on a label on the shipping container.

notes: Stress past any of these limits can destroy the part; long exposure at a limit can reduce its reliability and service life.
Input current: the two inputs are joined by a pair of opposed diodes. When the voltage between the inputs passes 0.7 V, the current into them has to be held under 40 mA.
Output short-circuit duration: with the output shorted without limit of time, a heat sink can be needed to hold the junction under its maximum temperature.
Operating temperature range: the C and I grades of LT6230, LT6231 and LT6232 all work from −40 °C to 85 °C.

Specified temperature range: C-grade parts meet their specifications over 0 °C to 70 °C; over −40 °C to 85 °C they are designed and characterized to meet them but are neither tested nor QA sampled. I-grade parts meet their specifications over −40 °C to 85 °C.

circuits.title: Low noise, low power instrumentation amplifier, gain 40
circuits.description: A three-amplifier instrumentation amplifier. The two halves of an LT6231 take the inputs on their noninverting pins; R2 and R3 from each output back to its inverting input, joined through the 10 Ω R1, set the front-end gain. A separate LT6202 with four 499 Ω resistors subtracts the two front-end outputs and references the result to ground. Overall gain is 40 with 5.1 MHz bandwidth on ±1.5 V to ±5 V; the whole circuit draws 10 mA and its input-referred noise is 5.8 µVRMS in an 8 MHz measurement bandwidth.

parts.note: dual; amplifier A on IN+, amplifier B on IN−

notes: AV = 40; BW = 5.1 MHz; VS = ±1.5 V to ±5 V; IS = 10 mA; EN = 5.8 µVRMS input referred, 8 MHz measurement bandwidth.

circuits.title: Single supply, low noise, low power bandpass filter with gain 10
circuits.description: A multiple-feedback bandpass filter on one LT6230 from a single supply. C1 couples the input into the R1/R2 junction; R1 returns to the output, R2 feeds the inverting input, and C2 runs from the inverting input to the output. R3 and R4 divide V+ in half for the noninverting input and C3 bypasses that node to ground; V+ has a 0.1 µF bypass to ground and ENABLE is grounded. With the values shown the centre is 1 MHz with 20 dB of gain there; the −3 dB bandwidth is f0/2.5; input-referred noise is 4 µVRMS and supply current 3.7 mA at V+ = 5 V. Other centre frequencies follow f0 = (732 Ω/R) MHz with R = R1 = R2, up to 1 MHz.
notes: f0 = 1/(2πRC) = 1 MHz with C = √(C1·C2) and R = R1 = R2; f−3dB = f0/2.5; AV = 20 dB at f0; EN = 4 µVRMS input referred; IS = 3.7 mA at V+ = 5 V.
V− of U1 is the ground of the single supply.

circuits.title: Low noise, low power, single supply instrumentation amplifier with gain 100
circuits.description: An AC-coupled instrumentation amplifier on one supply. Each input arrives through a 1 µF capacitor at the noninverting pin of an LT6230-10 and is returned through 511 Ω (R6, R5) to a mid-supply point set by R13 and R14 (2k each) and bypassed by C4 (10 µF); R5 and R6 are the input resistance. U1 and U2 each have 511 Ω feedback and 30.9 Ω to a common node that C2 (2200 pF) takes to ground; each stage has a gain of R2/R1 + 1. The LT6230 U3 then takes the difference with gain R10/R15, its R16/R12 arm returned to the mid-supply point, with 68 pF (C8, C9) across R10 and R12. The output is 100 × (VIN2 − VIN1) from 310 Hz to 11 MHz, with 20 µVRMS input-referred noise and 10.5 mA total supply current at 5 V. All three ENABLE pins are tied to ground.
notes: VOUT = 100 (VIN2 − VIN1); GAIN = (R2/R1 + 1)(R10/R15) with R1 = R3, R2 = R4, R10 = R12, R15 = R16; input resistance = R5 = R6; f−3dB = 310 Hz to 11 MHz; EN = 20 µVRMS input referred; IS = 10.5 mA at VS = 5 V, 0 V.

circuits.title: Low power avalanche photodiode transimpedance amplifier
circuits.description: An LT6230 on ±5 V turns the current of an avalanche photodiode into a voltage. The photodiode's cathode sits at about 200 V of bias and its anode feeds the inverting input; R1 (1.5k) from output to that input sets a gain of −1.5 kΩ, so VOUT = −IPD × 1.5k, and C1 (4.7 pF) across R1 keeps the loop stable and settling clean. R2, also 1.5k, from the noninverting input to ground cancels the DC error of the bias current, and C2 (0.1 µF) across it shunts R2's thermal noise. The 1.5k resistor carries 5 nV/√Hz or 3.4 pA/√Hz of its own noise, more than the amplifier's 1.1 nV/√Hz and 2.4 pA/√Hz. Measured: output offset 280 µV (500 µV typical), 17 ns rise time for about 20 MHz of bandwidth, 1.1 mVP-P output noise in a 100 MHz bandwidth, 3.3 mA supply current. ENABLE is grounded.

operation.text: LT6230 (single), LT6231 (dual) and LT6232 (quad) are unity-gain stable, rail-to-rail output op amps with 1.1 nV/√Hz input noise and at most 3.5 mA per amplifier, 215 MHz gain-bandwidth and 70 V/µs slew rate on ±5 V. The LT6230-10 is a single for closed-loop gains of 10 or more, with 1450 MHz gain-bandwidth. They run from 3 V to 12.6 V total and are specified at 3.3 V, 5 V and ±5 V. The output comes within 50 mV of each rail. The noise density times the square root of supply current is 1.9 per amplifier. Packages: the singles in the 1 mm high 6-lead TSOT-23, the dual in 8-pin SO and 3 mm × 3 mm DFN, the quad in 16-pin narrow SSOP.

The input stage is a low-noise NPN pair, Q1 and Q2. The current mirror Q3/Q4 turns their differential signal into one output, and the mirror transistors are degenerated so they add little noise. C1 lowers the unity-crossing frequency to steady the loop without cutting the gain-bandwidth, which CM sets. A differential drive stage feeds the output pair Q5 and Q6, which swing rail to rail. ESD diodes run from every input and the output to both supplies.

Opposed diodes D1 and D2 between +IN and −IN clamp the differential input at ±0.7 V. No resistors sit in series with the input transistors, because they would add noise: 100 Ω in each input alone contributes 1.8 nV/√Hz and raises the total from 1.1 nV/√Hz to 2.1 nV/√Hz. Above ±0.7 V of differential input the steady diode current must be held to ±40 mA, which takes 25 Ω of series resistance per volt beyond 0.7 V. The diodes withstand the brief currents of slew-rate overdrive and clipping with no resistors.

Measured as a unity-gain follower on ±2.5 V with the input driven beyond the supplies. Driven low, the output reaches V−: current source I1 saturates and the drive stage takes Q6 into saturation. Driven high, Q2 saturates into the Q3/Q4 mirror and the output starts to phase-invert; D2 then conducts from the source through the feedback connection, holding the output one diode drop under the input (the test generator current-limited near 20 mA). At closed-loop gains of 2 and above, very heavy overdrive can invert the output; it does not happen with overdrive of 0.5 V or less past the rails.
Reverse-biased ESD diodes on all inputs and outputs conduct without limit if a pin is forced past either supply. A transient current of up to 100 mA does no damage.

The input voltage noise equals the thermal noise of 75 Ω. For the lowest noise keep RS + RG||RFB at or below 75 Ω; at exactly 75 Ω the total is 1.55 nV/√Hz. Below 75 Ω the amplifier dominates; from 75 Ω to about 3 kΩ the resistors' thermal noise dominates; above about 3 kΩ the amplifier's noise current times the resistance takes over. The eN·√ISUPPLY figure of 1.9 per amplifier compares with up to 13.5 for amplifiers of similar noise.

ENABLE on the LT6230 and LT6230-10 cuts supply current to 10 µA maximum. Low on the pin gives normal operation; shutdown needs the pin within 0.35 V of V+. Plain gate logic can drive it. Where the logic has its own supply, an open-drain output with a pull-up resistor holds the amplifier off. Turn-on is about 300 ns and turn-off about 41 µs (VS = 5 V, RL = 1k).
Output leakage when disabled is very low, but if the output is driven more than a diode drop above the input, current flows through the input protection diodes D1 and D2.
